theory.title: Introducing Regular Past Verbs
theory.intro: This lesson introduces regular past verbs as tools to report completed actions in projects, lessons and technical tasks.
content: Many common verbs form the past with -ed.

At this stage, the learner should focus on meaning first: something happened and is complete.
The context remains practical and connected to study work, code work and platform activities.
The goal is a short action report, not complex storytelling.

theory.title: Using Did to Ask About Past Actions

theory.title: Integrating Past Actions in a Technical Report
theory.intro: This lesson reviews the core past-action language of the phase and asks the learner to combine regular and irregular verbs more fluently.
content: A strong technical report often combines more than one action.
At this stage, the learner should move beyond isolated sentences and produce short integrated updates.
Useful verbs include regular forms such as worked, fixed, tested and irregular forms such as found, made and did.
The goal is practical fluency, not complexity.
The context should remain anchored in tasks, bugs, files, code and small project work.

I found the file and made a small change.

I did the review and checked the final file.

Incorrect: I find the file and made a change. → Correct: I found the file and made a change.

theory.title: Opening a Post-Mortem with the Incident
theory.intro: This lesson teaches the learner how to begin a post-mortem or sprint retrospective by naming the technical problem clearly.
content: A good retrospective usually begins with the incident itself.
Use short direct sentences to say what broke or failed.
This opening gives the listener the context needed for the rest of the explanation.
At this stage, the learner should sound direct and technically clear.
The goal is to establish the problem before talking about actions and solutions.
examples: The server crashed during the test.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: Yesterday, the build fail. → Correct: Yesterday, the build failed.
Incorrect: The server crash during the test. → Correct: The server crashed during the test.
Incorrect: The database locked. → Correct: The database was locked.

theory_pt.intro: Esta lição ensina o aluno a começar um post-mortem ou sprint retrospective nomeando claramente o problema técnico.

Essa abertura dá ao ouvinte o contexto necessário para o resto da explicação.
Nesta fase, o aluno deve soar direto e tecnicamente claro.
O objetivo é estabelecer o problema antes de falar de ações e soluções.
examples: O servidor caiu durante o teste.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: Yesterday, the build fail. → Correto: Yesterday, the build failed.

theory.title: From Incident to Response
theory.intro: This lesson helps the learner move from describing the problem to describing what was discovered and what action followed.
content: A post-mortem is not only about the failure. It is also about the response.
Use found to report discovery and made or fixed to report action.
These verbs create the bridge between the incident and the solution process.
The learner should sound active and solution-oriented.
The goal is a short, clear transition from problem to action.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I find the bug yesterday. → Correct: I found the bug.
Incorrect: I maked a small change. → Correct: I made a small change.

Esses verbos criam a ponte entre o incidente e o processo de solução.
O aluno deve soar ativo e orientado à solução.
O objetivo é uma transição curta e clara do problema para a ação.

theory.title: Adding Tool, Method and Sequence to the Retrospective
theory.intro: This lesson integrates the explanatory layers of the phase into the retrospective: what tool was used, what method was used and in what order the steps happened.
content: A strong technical retrospective explains more than action. It explains process.
Use I used... for tool, by + verb-ing for method, and sequencing words such as first, then and finally for order.
These elements make the learner sound more explanatory and less robotic.
The learner should keep the process short, clear and believable.
The goal is procedural technical explanation in beginner-friendly language.
examples: I fixed it by testing the code.
First, I checked the file. Then, I tested the API.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I fixed it by test the code. → Correct: I fixed it by testing the code.
Incorrect: I use the debugger yesterday. → Correct: I used the debugger.
Incorrect: Finally, it work. → Correct: Finally, it worked.

theory_pt.title: Adicionando Ferramenta, Método e Sequência à Retrospectiva
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição integra as camadas explicativas da fase à retrospectiva: que ferramenta foi usada, que método foi usado e em que ordem os passos aconteceram.
content: Uma retrospectiva técnica forte explica mais do que ação. Ela explica processo.
Use I used... para ferramenta, by + verbo com -ing para método e palavras de sequência como first, then e finally para ordem.
Esses elementos fazem o aluno soar mais explicativo e menos robótico.
O aluno deve manter o processo curto, claro e crível.
O objetivo é explicação técnica procedural em linguagem acessível para iniciante.
examples: Eu corrigi isso testando o código.
Primeiro, eu verifiquei o arquivo. Depois, eu testei a API.

theory.title: Building My Sprint Retrospective / Post-Mortem Report
theory.intro: The final lesson of Week 24 integrates the full communication block of Phase 5 into a compact technical retrospective.
content: A good sprint retrospective or post-mortem includes four core elements: the incident, the discovery, the method and the resolution sequence.
This lesson closes an eight-week cycle focused on reporting actions in the past and explaining simple technical problem solving.
The learner should now be able to explain what broke, what was found, what was used and how the solution happened step by step.
The language should stay simple, but the report should sound coherent and professional.
The goal is not advanced engineering vocabulary. It is structured technical communication.
examples: I used the debugger and fixed it by testing the code.
First, I checked the file. Then, I tested the API. Finally, it worked.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: Yesterday, the build fail. → Correct: Yesterday, the build failed.
Incorrect: I find the bug. → Correct: I found the bug.
Incorrect: I fixed it by test the code. → Correct: I fixed it by testing the code.
Incorrect: Finally, it work. → Correct: Finally, it worked.

theory_pt.title: Construindo Meu Sprint Retrospective / Post-Mortem Report
theory_pt.intro: A lição final da Week 24 integra todo o bloco de comunicação da Fase 5 em uma retrospectiva técnica compacta.
content: Uma boa sprint retrospective ou post-mortem inclui quatro elementos centrais: o incidente, a descoberta, o método e a sequência de resolução.
Esta lição fecha um ciclo de oito semanas focado inteiramente em relatar ações no passado e explicar resolução simples de problema técnico.
O aluno agora deve ser capaz de explicar o que quebrou, o que foi encontrado, o que foi usado e como a solução aconteceu passo a passo.
A linguagem deve permanecer simples, mas o reporte deve soar coerente e profissional.
O objetivo não é vocabulário avançado de engenharia. É comunicação técnica estruturada.
examples: Eu usei o depurador e corrigi isso testando o código.
Primeiro, eu verifiquei o arquivo. Depois, eu testei a API. Finalmente, funcionou.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: Yesterday, the build fail. → Correto: Yesterday, the build failed.
Incorreto: I find the bug. → Correto: I found the bug.
Incorreto: I fixed it by test the code. → Correto: I fixed it by testing the code.
Incorreto: Finally, it work. → Correto: Finally, it worked.
